sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages; signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t)
sources.locator: Section 3.2 'The stretch factor is the Doppler shift' pp. 55-57, Section 3.3 'Combination of velocities' pp. 57-59, and Sections 6.4-6.6 pp. 134-141 (6.4.1 duality pp. 134-136, 6.4.2 change of basis p. 136, 6.5.1 Doppler shift p. 137, 6.5.2 aberration pp. 137-139, 6.6.1 phase velocity pp. 140-141, 6.6.2 group velocity pp. 141-142); the load-bearing pages were re-read in the extracted text of this exact 246-page revision

contents.name: Section 3.2 'The stretch factor is the Doppler shift': the factor D(v) = sqrt((1+v)/(1-v)), the longitudinal shift, the identity D(v)D(-v) = 1 and the transverse remark '1/gamma interpreted as time dilation'
contents.support: Absorbed into the theorem's clause (iii) (longitudinal exact factors, converted to the (-+++) sign and beta conventions) and clause (iv) (the transverse shift is present; the protocol-dependence of the factor gamma versus 1/gamma is added because the source does not distinguish the two transversality frames).

contents.name: Example 1 'Ives-Stilwell experiments' pp. 56-57: reported frequencies and uncertainties of the Saathoff et al. Li+ measurement
contents.reason: Reported experimental data with quoted uncertainties; the framework reserves primary-report and analysis work to the experimental-interface pair, and a textbook recap is secondary narrative that cannot back an experiment item here.

contents.name: Section 3.3 'Combination of velocities': composition of D factors, rapidity eta = ln D, v_c = (v1+v2)/(1+v1 v2) and the Bertozzi electron data in Example 2
contents.reason: Velocity composition and rapidity are supplied by the Lorentz-transformation page's boost-composition and rapidity items; the electron time-of-flight data are reported measurements reserved to the experimental interface, so neither belongs to this pair's wave inventory.

contents.name: Section 3.4 'No frame of reference moving at c': the boost parameter never reaches 1 and the light cone degenerates in the limit
contents.reason: This is a property of the boost family and the closed future cone already carried by the Lorentz-transformation and primitives pages; this pair adds no wave-specific claim and must not duplicate the supplier statements.

contents.name: Section 6.4.1 'Duality' and Examples 4-5 pp. 134-136: vector-to-covector duality by flipping the timelike component, dual of dual, and the matrix form with g and g^{-1}
contents.support: The duality algebra is absorbed into the metric-duality lemma with the signature conversion; his self-inverse component recipe (flip the spacelike component) is the lemma's clause (d), (k^sharp)^0 = -k_0 and (k^sharp)^i = k_i in an eta-orthonormal basis.

contents.name: Section 6.4.2 'Change of basis' p. 136: covectors transform under the inverse Lorentz transformation, and the row/column picture of the scalar product
contents.support: Absorbed into the component law k'_a = (B(-beta))^b_a k_b for a covector under the passive boost, with the matrix entries computed from the inverse boost.

contents.name: Section 6.5.1 'Doppler shift' p. 137: the frequency four-vector (omega, omega cos theta, omega sin theta) must be lightlike, and omega' = gamma omega (1 + v cos theta) after the inverse boost
contents.support: The theorem's clauses (i)-(iii) state the general and longitudinal Doppler results in the library's (-+++) and passive-boost conventions; the source's formula is recovered with its theta measured from the incoming line of sight, which is the theorem's beta . s with s the propagation direction.

contents.name: Section 6.5.2 'Aberration' pp. 137-139: tan theta' = sin theta / (gamma (cos theta + v)) and the claimed-limits discussion
contents.support: Converted to the equivalent cos theta' = (cos theta - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta) in the library's conventions and proved as clause (v); the source's discussion of alternative emission theories is not harvested as a claim.

contents.name: Example 6 'A test of special relativity' p. 139: Heckmann's photographic plates and the reported relative shift 0.00 +/- 0.06 arcsec
contents.reason: A reported measurement with an uncertainty and a specific apparatus; experiment authoring requires the primary report, calibration and statistical analysis, which the framework reserves to the experimental-interface pair, not a secondary retelling.

contents.name: Example 7 'The view of an ultrarelativistic observer' pp. 139-140: aberration-distorted optical appearance of a cube, light-travel-time rendering and the warning that optical appearance is not length contraction
contents.reason: Optical appearance of extended bodies requires light-travel-time rendering of many emitted rays and is explicitly distinguished from the plane-wave frequency and direction transformation; it is outside this pair's declared wave inventory.

contents.name: Section 6.6.1 'Phase velocity' pp. 140-141: the phase velocity is not a velocity, the phase information does not determine the propagation direction except for waves at c, and for light the dual vector gives the direction
contents.support: The exception at speed c is exactly the future null wave covector k with its raised vector k^sharp as the propagation direction; the worked example verifies by exact algebra that the level sets are null hyperplanes containing the line of k^sharp.

contents.name: Section 6.6.2 'Group velocity' pp. 141-142: modulated waves, dispersion relations C = 0 and the distinction between phase and group velocities as signal speed
contents.reason: Group velocity requires a modulated wave packet and a dispersion model, and signal-speed claims need a separate analysis; this pair's model is a single ideal monochromatic plane wave with no dispersion, so the result has no destination here.

sources.title: A. Einstein, 'Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Koerper', Annalen der Physik 322 (10) 891-921 (1905); Section 7 'Theorie des Dopplerschen Prinzips und der Aberration', journal pp. 910-912; proofread full-text transcription of the original (German Wikisource, Einstein-Elektrodynamik.djvu, transcription pages 20-22 of 31)
sources.locator: Section 7, journal pp. 910-912: transformed wave phase Phi' = omega'(tau - (a' xi + b' eta + c' zeta)/V) with omega' = omega beta (1 - a v/V), the Doppler principle nu' = nu (1 - cos(phi) v/V)/sqrt(1-(v/V)^2), the longitudinal special case nu' = nu sqrt((1-v/V)/(1+v/V)), the aberration law cos(phi') = (cos(phi) - v/V)/(1 - (v/V) cos(phi)), the case phi = pi/2, and the amplitude transformation at the end of the section

contents.name: Transformed plane-wave representation and phase in the moving system: Phi' = omega'(tau - (a' xi + b' eta + c' zeta)/V) with omega' = omega beta (1 - a v/V), a' = (a - v/V)/(1 - a v/V), b' and c' rescaled by 1/(beta(1 - a v/V))
contents.support: The phase transformation is exactly the covector component law for the same affine phase function; the theorem re-derives the same coefficients from lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation in the library's (-+++) conventions and identifies a = cos(phi) = s_1.

contents.name: Doppler principle for arbitrary velocities: nu' = nu (1 - cos(phi) v/V)/sqrt(1 - (v/V)^2), with phi the angle between the source-observer line and the observer's velocity
contents.support: Identical to the theorem's general formula omega' = gamma (1 - beta . s) omega once cos(phi) = beta_hat . s, since the source-observer line is the propagation direction; the theorem states the same result with the frame and observer conventions of this library.

contents.name: Longitudinal special case phi = 0: nu' = nu sqrt((1 - v/V)/(1 + v/V)), with the remark that this differs from the customary view in the limit
contents.support: The theorem's clause (iii) s = beta_hat gives exactly omega' = omega sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)); the limit remark is not part of the library's claim.

contents.name: Aberration law: cos(phi') = (cos(phi) - v/V)/(1 - (v/V) cos(phi)), and the special case phi = pi/2 giving cos(phi') = -v/V
contents.support: The theorem's clause (v) states the identical formula with |beta| = v/V and proves the map properties; the pi/2 special case is included there.

contents.name: Amplitude transformation A'^2 = A^2 (1 - (v/V) cos(phi))^2/sqrt(1 - (v/V)^2) and the remark about intensity for an observer approaching at speed V
contents.reason: The amplitude and intensity transformation presupposes an electromagnetic field-energy model and belongs to the electromagnetism framework's radiation pages; this pair's reservation is the ideal-wave frequency and direction kinematics, which adopt no amplitude or intensity model.

sources.title: S. Murugesh, 'Relativity - Special Theory' (IIST course notes for PH33003/PH43017, last update 2009-02-18, 31 PDF pages)
sources.locator: Chapter 6 'Waves' pp. 25-28: plane-wave description and phase velocity (6.1) p. 25, phase matching and the wave four-vector (6.2)-(6.5) pp. 25-26, Section 6.1.1 longitudinal Doppler effect p. 26, Section 6.1.2 transverse Doppler effect p. 27, Section 6.2 aberration p. 28; a second independent four-vector treatment of the whole Doppler/aberration complex, pinned to replace the coverage shortfall recorded for SR07 in research/first-principles-2026-10-03/relativity/scaffold/prose-scaffold.md

contents.name: Chapter 6 opening: a plane wave Phi = Phi_0 sin(k . r - omega_k t) is characterized by wave vector, angular frequency and amplitude, with phase velocity v_k = omega_k/|k|
contents.support: Absorbed as the affine phase theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const with kappa = (omega/c) s; the amplitude and the general phase velocity are not part of this pair's model, and the light case omega = c|kappa| is the null condition of the frame-data lemma.

contents.name: Phase matching k . r - omega_k t = k' . r' - omega'_k' t' and the wave four-vector k = (omega_k/c; k), null for light in vacuum (equations (6.2)-(6.5))
contents.support: The phase is a scalar function on A, so its chart independence is automatic in this library's formulation; the lemma verifies the equivalent component statement, and the null condition eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = 0 with future k^sharp is the light case of the wave four-vector.

contents.name: Section 6.1.1 'Longitudinal Doppler effect': omega'_k' = gamma_0 omega_k (1 - k_hat . beta_0), with the red-shifted factor sqrt((1-beta_0)/(1+beta_0)) and the blue-shifted reciprocal
contents.support: Identical to the theorem's general formula and clause (iii) after identifying k_hat with the propagation direction s and beta_0 with the boost parameter; the notes' sign of beta_0 is the same receding/approaching convention.

contents.name: Section 6.1.2 'Transverse Doppler effect': omega'_k' = omega_k/gamma_0 for the wave vector transverse to the motion in the observer's frame (equations (6.13)-(6.14))
contents.support: This is the second of the two transversality protocols stated in the theorem's clause (iv) (beta . s = |beta|^2, equivalently s' . beta_hat = 0) with the factor 1/gamma, and the worked example computes it with the protocol that gives gamma in the other frame; the pair keeps both protocols explicit because the sources choose opposite conventions.

contents.name: Section 6.2 'Aberration': sin(theta') = sin(theta)/(gamma_0 (1 + beta_0 cos(theta))) and the qualitative statement that the angle decreases for an observer moving toward the source
contents.support: Equivalent to the theorem's cos theta' = (cos theta - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta) after converting the notes' coordinate and beta sign conventions (their +beta_0 direction corresponds to the library's -beta); clause (v) states and proves the exact map and the pi/2 special case.

canonical.name: Observer frequency as minus the phase rate with respect to the observer's proper time, with the sign convention omega_n = -c k(n) = -k(U_o) > 0
The two transversality protocols of the transverse Doppler effect (factors gamma and 1/gamma) and the requirement to name the frame
Phase level sets are null hyperplanes containing the propagation line k^sharp, verified by exact algebra
